name: Bell/Marino ELF epoch probe: 2-s epochs of 10 Hz and 1.5 Hz, 5 s apart
origin: Bell, Marino, Chesson (Louisiana State University Medical Center), 1991-1996
summary: Research probe after Bell, Marino and Chesson's EEG studies: 2-s epochs of a 10 Hz, then a 1.5 Hz sine field on all eight ring coils in phase, each followed by 5 s without field, to look for EEG changes at the stimulus frequency. Bell et al. 1994 reported such changes in a uniform field of 0.2 to 0.4 gauss rms (28 to 57 uT peak); this helmet gives 5 uT at 20 mm from each coil, so only the timing is copied.
notes: In Bell et al. 1994 'a trial consisted of the presentation of the magnetic field for 2 sec, followed by an interstimulus period of 5 sec' (J Neurol Sci p.3 [28]). The control was the 2 s just before each field epoch, in a fixed order (p.3 [28]). Each of the 19 subjects had one frequency, 10 Hz (subjects 1 to 10) or 1.5 Hz (11 to 19), in blocks of 50 trials at 0.2 and at 0.4 gauss, plus a 0.8 gauss block to measure coil pickup (Table 1 p.2 [27]; p.3 [28]). Two coils of 130 cm diameter and 250 turns, 65 cm apart, gave a field uniform within 5% over head and upper chest (p.1-2 [26-27]). This program plays both frequencies in one run at one level: 10 min of 10 Hz epochs, then 10 min of 1.5 Hz epochs, on all eight ring coils in phase. Each 2-s epoch holds whole cycles (20 at 10 Hz, 3 at 1.5 Hz). There is no fade, so field epochs start 0, 7, 14 ... s into each phase. A 10-min phase holds 85 trials; Bell's 100 trials would take 11 min 40 s. The 0.8 gauss pickup block is missing, so test the recording chain with a phantom. Eight radial coils do not make a uniform field. The paper calls its strongest block '0.8 gauss rms' (p.2 [27]), so 0.2 to 0.4 gauss is read as rms, 28 to 57 uT peak; the paper does not label the two lower values. This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 5 uT it is 5.7 to 11 times weaker there (3.4 to 6.7 times at the helmet's maximum). The results come from one lab, and Marino et al. 1996 reported high false-negative rates for the method (42% for a 0.8 G field). EEG changes at the stimulus frequency are exactly where coil pickup appears, so run the program blinded against sham (the app's Blind option). The induced electric field at 10 Hz is about 1 uV/m; a positive result would be extraordinary. The 10-min after-effect test is the program lowfield-bell-elf-epoch-probe-aftereffect. Not for people with epilepsy; stop if you feel unwell.
setting: Seated, eyes closed, in a dark room, with EEG at C3, C4, P3, P4, O1 and O2. Compare each 2-s field epoch with the 2 s just before it, within each subject, as Bell did (Bell 1994 J Neurol Sci p.3 [28]).
schedule: One run per sitting; repeat with blinded sham runs of the same program.
source: Bell et al. 1994, J Neurol Sci (1.5 and 10 Hz, 2-s epochs) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8064317/ ; Bell et al. 1992, Electroencephalogr Clin Neurophysiol (2-s epochs, central and parietal changes) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1281085/ ; Bell, Marino, Chesson & Struve 1991, Lancet 338:1521 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1683938/ ; Marino et al. 1996, J Neurol Sci (false-negative rates) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8994110/ ; Bell et al. 1994, Neuroreport (10 Hz after-effect) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8003686/
